$comment: Copy to config.json and edit. Everything the harness needs to run lives
here — the scripts hold no project-specific knowledge.
Paths may use ~ and are expanded at runtime.
Every value below is a placeholder: replace it with your own.

scope.$comment: What to mine. Either a parent issue/epic, or a label, or both.

owner.$comment: Who the work is for. Used to filter eligible items and to assign.

tracker.$exclude_labels: Items carrying any of these are dropped before the model sees them — the 'needs a human decision first' escape hatch.

statuses.$comment: The only statuses the broker will move an item to. Anything else is rejected, so a run can never mark work Done or reopen something. Use your board's exact names.

tracker.$statuses: in_review requires evidence: the queued action must carry a pull request URL under project.repo, and the broker verifies with `gh pr view` that it exists before transitioning. Set in_review to null on a board with no review column.

run.$schedule: local time, HH:MM — install.sh turns this into the launchd calendar entry

$comment: Commands run inside each worktree before pushing. The harness never passes --no-verify, so the hooks must actually run: hook_probe proves they resolve, and it is a command rather than a path for the reason in $hook_probe below.
These examples assume a pnpm/turbo monorepo — replace them with your project's own.
verify.$env_sync: Optional. Runs before install when the project needs gitignored .env files a fresh worktree does not have. Set to null if it does not.
verify.$hook_probe: A command, not a path: git resolves core.hooksPath relative to the worktree root, so probing a literal path can pass in one checkout and fail in another. Set core.hooksPath to an ABSOLUTE path in the main checkout and every worktree inherits working hooks — husky prepare cannot run in a worktree anyway, it writes the shared .git/config.
verify.$hooks_path: Absolute path the runner pins core.hooksPath to before every run. Worktrees share .git/config, and hook installers (husky) rewrite that key to a RELATIVE path on every install — which resolves to a directory a fresh worktree does not have, so hooks silently stop running. Pinning it absolute makes every worktree inherit working hooks; HUSKY=0 in verify.install stops the install from undoing it. Set to null for repos without this problem.

$comment: Writes are confined to workspace_root plus extra_write_paths.
Network egress is confined to allowed_domains. Both are enforced by the
Claude Code sandbox, not by the prompt.
sandbox.$allowed_domains: Keep this as short as the run allows. 'your-schema-host.example.com' stands for whatever host your pre-push checks have to reach (a codegen or schema-introspection endpoint, say); drop it if they reach nothing.
sandbox.$weaker_network_isolation: Required by Go CLIs (gh, acli) that verify TLS through trustd. See docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md.

pull_request.$labels: Applied to every PR the job opens, and ensured to exist on the code host before each run — gh pr create fails outright if a label is missing.

notify.$command: Shell command receiving $PC_TITLE and $PC_BODY. Null uses the platform default (osascript on macOS). Set to a custom command to route elsewhere.
